content: Adolescents and young individuals should restrict their dietary protein intake to levels recommended for their specific age group to avoid potential renal strain or other health complications. Conduct annual screening for albuminuria by measuring the albumin-to-creatinine ratio to detect early signs of kidney damage or dysfunction. Annually assess the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) to monitor kidney function and identify any decline in renal performance. If the albumin-to-creatinine ratio is elevated but the eGFR remains within the normal range, initiate treatment with angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) to mitigate further kidney damage. In cases where nephropathy progresses or the eGFR shows a significant decline, refer the patient to a nephrologist for specialized evaluation and management.
